![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131516/assets/84806884f843154c17c338eef0f50d83cae049aece675450e21e58dade6a9f34.png)

Consider the set $A$ shown above. The interior of $A$ is 

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,\bbox[5px,border: 1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAA}}\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131516/assets/ce268d8b396ea63227734c1edd6b876bb0fe9755fa12a3b75be90c6ef4af5af3.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131516/assets/84780a84406a3fd0e281737b979887e0de6b1e9fe39d440f379fbb2b84e80a3b.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,{x}^{2}-1<y<0\}.
$$
